name: Armillaria ostoyae

ecology.substrate: conifer roots and stumps; soil between them

notes: Spreads by rhizomorphs and directly root to root, killing trees in expanding circles; it glows [8]. The Oregon individual covers 965 ha, with isolates up to 3,810 m apart and an age of 1,900 to 8,650 years [6]. Genome reported (unchecked).

tip_speed.note: spread through forest of 0.22 to 1.3 m/year (three studies compiled, snippet); the middle, 0.76 m/year, as a year-round average. A stand-scale front rate, not a measured tip speed

uptake_rate.note: tuning value tied to tip speed
